title: Head, tail, back, belly

objective.text: Name the three axes of the flat week-3 embryonic disc.

body.general: Which end of a flat disc is the head? Its head–tail and back–belly directions are fixed before the body's layers start to form [f1]. Head to tail (cranial–caudal) is the long axis: a groove, the primitive streak, forms at the tail end, and the head end is opposite [f2,f3]. Back to belly (dorsal–ventral) runs through the disc: the upper side is the back [f4]. Left and right are the embryo's own sides, not yours [f5].
body.mbbs: The disc has cranial–caudal and dorsal–ventral axes before the primitive streak appears [f1]. The cranial–caudal axis is the long axis: the streak forms in the caudal midline, and the cranial end lies opposite it [f2,f3]. The dorsal–ventral axis runs through the disc: dorsal is the upper side and ventral the lower side [f4]. The left–right axis is set while the layers form and always means the embryo's own left and right [f5].

facts.text: The head–tail and back–belly axes are already set before the primitive streak appears.
The primitive streak first shows in the caudal midline of the disc; its cranial end is the primitive node.
The streak marks the long axis: it lies at the caudal (tail) end, and the cranial (head) end is opposite it.
Dorsal is the epiblast side, facing the amniotic cavity; ventral is the hypoblast side, facing the yolk sac.
Left and right are set during gastrulation; they are the embryo's own left and right sides.

misconceptions.wrong: Left and right mean the viewer's left and right.
misconceptions.right: They are the embryo's own sides, whichever way you look at it.

misconceptions.wrong: The groove (primitive streak) forms at the head end.
misconceptions.right: It forms in the caudal midline; the head end is opposite it.

checks.prompt: The long axis of the disc, from head end to tail end, is called the…
checks.why: Cranial means toward the head and caudal toward the tail; the streak marks the caudal end.

options: The embryo's own left and right
Whichever side is drawn on the left
checks.why: Left and right are always the embryo's own sides, however you look at it.

checks.prompt: The axis that runs from the back side to the belly side is called the…
checks.why: Dorsal means the back (the upper side of the disc); ventral means the belly side.

checks.prompt: Where on the disc does the primitive streak form?
options: At the tail (caudal) end, in the midline
Along the rim of the disc
checks.why: The streak forms in the caudal midline, so the head end is the opposite end.

adult: These three axes become the body's own head-to-toe, back-to-front and left–right directions [f1,f5].

remember.q: Which way does the long axis of the disc run?
remember.a: Head (cranial) to tail (caudal); the streak marks the tail end [f3].

remember.q: Which side of the disc is dorsal?
